text:
Jordan (eng-platform): Quick question — for Private deployments: what's the recommended pattern for operator/ops tokens that sometimes need cross-org access vs the per-project API keys we already surface? Thinking about revocation and audits.
Maria (eng-security): Prefer no global, permanent operator keys. Instead scoped tokens with capability flags (e.g. can_mint_bridge, org_admin) and short TTLs where possible.
Sam (eng-sre): For integrations (alert sinks, metrics exporters) many vendors only accept a single API key. How would scoped tokens work there?
Jordan (eng-platform): Option: mint short-lived "bridge" tokens for the integration that carry explicit claims about which org/project they're acting for. TTL like 1h and logged on creation.
Chris (security): +1 to bridge tokens. Also ensure actor provenance is preserved — runtime should attach an X-Actor header (or similar) so we can trace request->tenant mapping even when using bridge tokens.
Maria (eng-security): That implies runtime changes: token minting service should return both the token and a canonical actor claim. We need an audit_id for each mint event.
Sam (eng-sre): Edge case: worker pools that fan out calls for many tenants — creating per-tenant tokens is expensive. We could have a proxy that maps a single long-lived proxy key to short-lived per-tenant bridge tokens issued on demand.
Jordan (eng-platform): Proxy is sensible. Guardrails: no permanent storage of bridge tokens for external sinks; rotate proxy key daily or require HSM-backed keys for long-lived secrets.
Chris (security): Tradeoff: very frequent rotation increases churn and monitoring load. Proposal: "expiring but renewable" tokens — TTL short, with a renewal endpoint that enforces tenant + caller checks and emits events.
Maria (eng-security): API surface proposal:

```
POST /tokens/mint
{
  "subject": "service:alert-sink",
  "scope": ["ingest:events"],
  "ttl": 3600,
  "context": {"org_id": "org-123", "requested_by": "jordan"}
}
```

Response includes token, audit_id, expires_at.
Jordan (eng-platform): Also need admin UI: "Revoke all bridge tokens for org-123" and org-level audit view filtered by audit_id.
Sam (eng-sre): Migration question: Dedicated customers may still have long-lived keys stored in their systems. How do we migrate without breaking them?
Chris (security): Migration plan: accept legacy keys for read-only calls and warn in logs; provide tooling to batch-create bridge tokens and a shim/proxy so existing integrations can keep using one key but we back it with per-tenant attestations.
Maria (eng-security): Also add a permission gate: only principals with can_mint_bridge can call /tokens/mint for org-level subjects. That reduces accidental exposure.
Jordan (eng-platform): Follow-up action: draft a tiny RFC for the bridge token flow + runtime header change. I'll sketch the sequence diagram.
Sam (eng-sre): +1. Also add metrics: mint_count, renew_count, revoke_count, avg_ttl, failed_mint_rate.
Chris (security): Sounds good. We should also add a security review task for the proxy pattern (threat modelling for token exchange).
Maria (eng-security): :thumbsup: I'll start the RFC draft and include a compatibility section for Dedicated/private customers.
Jordan (eng-platform): Thanks — tagging next steps: @Maria to draft RFC, @Chris for threat model, @Sam for operational metrics.
